Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

optcompR 0.1.0

First release. optcompR is a solver independent modeling layer for mathematical optimization in R: models are written with ordinary R operators, classified with recorded evidence, lowered to sparse standard forms, solved by installed backends, and returned as standardized, independently checked results.

Modeling

  • Continuous, integer and binary decision variables, parameters and symmetric matrix variables (opt_variable(), opt_parameter(), opt_sym_variable()), with vectorized linear, quadratic and nonlinear expressions, sparse Matrix support, ranged constraints and named blocks. Matrix products follow the conformability rules of base R.
  • Cone constraints: second-order, exponential, power and positive semidefinite (opt_soc_constraint(), opt_exp_cone(), opt_pow_cone(), opt_psd_constraint()).
  • Indicator, SOS1, SOS2, complementarity and logical constraints (opt_indicator(), opt_sos1(), opt_sos2(), opt_implies(), opt_and(), opt_or()), reformulated exactly for solvers without native support.
  • External R functions with supplied, jaxR or labeled finite difference gradients (opt_function()).
  • Model inspection and editing: opt_copy(), opt_variables(), opt_constraints(), opt_special_constraints(), opt_delete_constraint(), opt_terms(), opt_degree(), opt_symbols(), opt_evaluate(), opt_standard_form() and opt_row_hessian().

Classification and solver selection

  • opt_classify() assigns the class (LP, MILP, QP, MIQP, QCQP, MIQCQP, SOCP, MISOCP, CONIC, NLP, MINLP) and records how convexity was established: structurally, numerically, or by disciplined convex programming rules with interval bounds for nonlinear expressions. When convexity cannot be proven the model is reported as "unknown", never guessed.
  • opt_solve() selects an installed backend whose R binding supports the class, preferring backends with global guarantees for nonconvex models. A model is never approximated to fit a solver; unsupported models are refused with the reason.

Backends

  • HiGHS (LP, MILP, convex QP, sensitivity ranging, warm starts and in-place updates across repeated solves), SCIP (global MIQCQP, MISOCP and polynomial NLP and MINLP by exact lifting to quadratic rows, native indicator and SOS constraints), Clarabel and SCS (LP, convex QP and conic programs, with cone multipliers), OSQP (convex QP), NLopt (local NLP), IPOPT with exact sparse Hessians (compiled in when available), NLP branch and bound for MINLP, and ROI plugins.
  • opt_register_solver() makes the backend contract public, so other solvers can be connected without changing optcompR.

Results and diagnostics

  • Standardized termination and point statuses that separate proven optimality, local optimality, early stops (including "gap_limit" with its gap and a valid bound) and infeasibility certificates.
  • Every returned point is checked against the model before it is reported feasible.
  • Duals are derivatives of the optimal value with a documented sign convention; opt_check() recomputes feasibility and the Karush Kuhn Tucker conditions, including conic ones, from the original expressions.
  • Exact gradients, Jacobians and Lagrangian Hessians.
  • opt_explain_infeasibility() reports which rows and bounds must move, and by how much, through a weighted elastic (L1) relaxation.
  • Exact feasibility checks and optimality certificates for LP and MILP through z3r (opt_z3_check(), opt_z3_certify()).

Sensitivity and analysis

  • Sensitivity ranging for LPs (opt_sensitivity()), fixed relaxations of mixed-integer results (opt_fixed_relaxation()) and parameter scenario sweeps (opt_scenarios()).
  • Derivatives of optimal solutions with respect to parameters (opt_solution_jacobian()), for smooth, conic and semidefinite programs.
  • Multiobjective scalarizations: opt_weighted(), opt_lexicographic() and opt_epsilon_constraint().

Robust and stochastic optimization

  • opt_robust_constraint() (box, ellipsoidal and budget uncertainty), opt_chance_constraint(), opt_cvar(), opt_expectation() and opt_worst_expectation(), all as exact reformulations.

Integrations

  • ODE least squares losses for modelcompR models with forward or adjoint gradients (opt_ode_loss()).
  • Conversion to and from symcompR expressions, to CVXR problems (opt_to_cvxr()), and export to MPS and LP files.

Documentation

  • Twenty vignettes and a pkgdown site.
